An arbitrary state type E, total real-valued functions psi and loss on natural time and E, an arbitrary sequence x, comparator u and terminal z, and a natural horizon T>0. No convexity, norm, optimizer, algorithm, probability or causal premise is required. Finite real arithmetic is a specialization: the full EReal/domain adapter remains separate. Indices are zero-based: source round s corresponds to t=s-1. G includes the current loss through t. Only the unscored coordinate T is spliced to z; all y(t)=x(t) for t<T. The original x(T) is unused. The interior drift has indices0..T-2; forT1 it is empty. T0 is not claimed.

Only the unscored coordinate T is spliced to z; all y(t)=x(t) for t<T. The original x(T) is unused. The interior drift has indices0..T-2; forT1 it is empty. T0 is not claimed.

Intuition
The terminal point appears once with a minus sign inside the last within-potential difference and once with a plus sign in the endpoint gap. Their cancellation explains why the scored regret does not depend on an unplayed endpoint.
Why it is needed
One shared algebraic component needed by labeled terminal corrections, not a complete regret theorem or source-container count.
Place in the proof
Finite-real corrected accounting near Theorem7.47 proof, PDF141–142; related Theorem15.31 terminal convention, PDF278–279. The full EReal adapter, actual optimistic-FTRL/BTRL producers, ghost attainment, support qualification, strong-convex stability, Young estimate and whole corrected7.47/15.31 bounds remain open. A positive arbitrary terminal gap cannot be discarded.
Proof and Lean reading notes
Proof idea
Put H_t(v)=sum_{i<t}loss_i(v), so G_t=psi_t+H_(t+1). The regularizer parts of the within-G sum, together with the interior drift, telescope to psi_0(y_0)-psi_(T-1)(z). The cumulative-loss parts telescope to sum_{t<T}loss_t(y_t)-H_T(z). Adding the final comparator regularizer minus the initial played regularizer and the retained G_(T-1)(z)-G_(T-1)(u) leaves exactly the regret. This is the mathematical cancellation argument, not a claimed implementation route.
Lean reading notes
E has no additional typeclass assumptions; psi/loss are real-valued and T>0 is the only propositional premise. The boundary regularizer difference is psi_(T-1)(u)-psi_0(y_0): final comparator regularizer minus initial played regularizer. Local y and G are definitions, not extra hypotheses. The exact Lean header and full-proof source link use the declaration fold; these notes do not claim a complete rendered source-proof graph. Selected actual compiled direct VALUE occurrences are Nat.recAux, Finset.sum_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_zero and Nat.sub_add_cancel. Occurrence does not establish logical necessity or a complete transitive graph; Nat.rec is not the exported direct constant. The source-only AND topology remains distinct from these implementation occurrences. panels.foldedExactStatement: theorem finite_regret_identity {E : Type*} (psi loss : ℕ → E → ℝ) (x : ℕ → E) (u z : E) (T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) : let y : ℕ → E := fun t => if t = T then z else x t let G : ℕ → E → ℝ := fun t v => psi t v + ∑ i ∈ range (t + 1), loss i v (∑ t ∈ range T, (loss t (y t) - loss t u)) = psi (T - 1) u - psi 0 (y 0) + (∑ t ∈ range T, (G t (y t) - G t (y (t + 1)))) + (∑ t ∈ range (T - 1), (psi t (y (t + 1)) - psi (t + 1) (y (t + 1)))) + G (T - 1) z - G (T - 1) u

Intuition
Existence supplies a minimizer. Convexity makes two minimizers satisfy opposite variational inequalities, forcing their squared separation to vanish.
Why it is needed
Algorithm 2.1 and Proposition 2.11 use a well-defined unique Euclidean projection. This theorem establishes existence and uniqueness before the existing choice-based definition.
Place in the proof
Well-definedness obligation for Orabona v10, printed p.12 / PDF p.24. The proof is library-derived; it is not an additional numbered source theorem.
Proof and Lean reading notes
Proof idea
Take a minimizer from Mathlib. For two minimizing points p and q, the variational characterization gives <z-p,q-p> <= 0 and <z-q,p-q> <= 0. Adding these inequalities gives ||q-p||^2 <= 0, hence q=p.
Lean reading notes
The source finite-dimensional Euclidean setting is generalized to a complete real inner-product space. Nonempty, closed and convex are explicit Domain fields; no boundedness or compactness is added. project_spec characterizes the unchanged selected projection using exactly this minimizer predicate. No executable solver, arbitrary Banach-space projection or nonexpansiveness claim. The proof reuses Mathlib exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_convex and norm_eq_iInf_iff_real_inner_le_zero; these upstream dependencies are not local declaration nodes.

import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Module
import Mathlib.Tactic

noncomputable section
open Finset
namespace BanditRL.OnlineCumulativePotential

import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Minimal
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# Projected online gradient descent

Orabona, arXiv:1912.13213v10, Algorithm 2.1, Proposition 2.11,
Lemma 2.12, Theorem 2.13 (constant step only), and Eq. (2.1).
Time `t = 0` denotes source round 1; `iterate ... T` is source `x_(T+1)`.
The Hilbert-space interfaces specialize to finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces.
Loss-dependent declarations below use the stronger historical `RegularLoss` predicate.
`OnlineGradientDescentSource` supplies the arbitrary-open source regularity interface
on the same algorithms. Projection and causal feasibility statements need no loss regularity.
-/

noncomputable section
open Set Finset
open scoped InnerProductSpace

namespace BanditRL.OnlineGradientDescent

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]

/-- A nonempty closed convex feasible set, independent of losses and comparators. -/
structure Domain (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] where
  carrier : Set E
  nonempty : carrier.Nonempty
  closed : IsClosed carrier
  convex : Convex ℝ carrier

/-- Every nonempty closed convex domain has a unique nearest point before any choice is made.
This establishes the well-definedness of the same projection used below. -/
